issue_context.title: Deployment rolling update hang during scaling
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

Deployment rolling update hangs if it is scaling at the same time.

#### What you expected to happen:

Changes in deployment's replicas do not block rolling update.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Supposing we have a deployment A with replicas 5, and the maxUnavailable is 1 and maxSurge is 0, then we trigger a rolling update (e.g. update image).
1. The deployment controller create a new replicaset (RS1) and scale down the old replicaset (RS2). The replicas of RS1 is 0, and RS2 will be scaled down to 4. Besides, there will be two annotations (i.e. DesiredReplicasAnnotation and MaxReplicasAnnotation) on RS2 with value 5.
2. Before deployment controller scales up the new replicaset RS1, we manually scale down the replicas of deployment A to 4.
3. The deployment controller will only try to sync the scaling event before rolling update.
4. The scale method in `DeploymentController` will not work because the replicas of active replicaset RS2 equals to deployment A, even though the annotation is set to 5.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
1.18.10
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
